summary.text: Daughter of Pelias and Anaxibia (`anaxibia-pelias`) at Iolcus — one of the Peliades named in Apollodorus beside Pisidice, Pelopia, Alcestis, and Acastus.

Homonym guard: not Hippothoe daughter of Mestor, whom Poseidon carried off to bear Taphius (Bibliotheca 2.4.5). As a Peliad she belongs to the daughters implicated in Medea's cauldron trick against Pelias.

story.text: Apollodorus counts Hippothoe among the daughters whom Pelias begot on Anaxibia, daughter of Bias — sister to Pisidice, Pelopia, Alcestis, and their brother Acastus in the Thessalian royal genealogy.

When Jason returned with Medea, the witch persuaded Pelias's daughters that an old ram boiled in her cauldron could renew life; trusting her, they minced and boiled their father — the homecoming vengeance Apollodorus and Ovid tell through the cauldron fraud.
